## TestVault.signCeremony() method

Run the full production signing ceremony — `createSigningKey` → `authorizeSigningKey` → `sign` — through the wrapped keeper in one call.

**Signature:**

```typescript
signCeremony(name: string, payload: string | Buffer, algorithm?: SigningAlgorithm): Promise<TestVaultSignCeremonyResult>;
```

## Exceptions

{<!-- -->SigningKeyAlreadyExistsError<!-- -->} If a signing key already exists under `name`<!-- -->.

## Remarks

This exercises the exact same call path a real consumer uses to sign with a vaultkeeper-managed key, so a test asserting on the returned `jws` is exercising production wiring, not an approximation of it. The private key never leaves the backend at any point in the ceremony (see `VaultKeeper.createSigningKey` in the `vaultkeeper` package).
